R19.5, the migration, in plain words. WHAT: the actual move, in six steps. (1) Copy traffic.jsonl to your Drive backup folder, encrypted, so the original survives whatever follows. (2) Read it into the new table, line by line, in file order, so row 1 is your oldest line. (3) Check the table's row count equals the file's line count; if not, stop. (4) From then on the node writes to the table, and the old file stays on disk untouched, read once if ever needed, never written again. (5) The way back, if any step fails: drop the table, and the node keeps writing the file as today. (6) Rewrite the comment in nodeStore.js that promises 'losing node.db costs a rebuild', citing your decision to rely on backups instead. WHY IT'S LAST: it's the only step that changes what your node does. It needs the table and indexes built (R19.3, R19.4), the tests off the file (R19.2, done), and a backup actually running (R19.1). WHAT YOU'LL SEE: your node works as before; lookups are faster; traffic.jsonl stops growing. STATE: decided, not built.

Right, and that's expected: no backup has ever run. Two steps are missing, both yours, because my permissions can't create the passphrase for you or schedule tasks on your machine. In a Windows terminal: (1) Create C:\Users\Andre\.spirit-backup-passphrase with a passphrase of 12+ characters, and keep a copy somewhere safe. (2) Run once by hand to see a file appear: node D:\SpiritOS\install\backup-windows\backup.js (3) Then schedule it hourly: schtasks /Create /SC HOURLY /TN "SpiritOS backup" /TR "D:\SpiritOS\install\backup-windows\run.cmd" After step 2 a file named spirit-backup-<date>.tgz.enc is in that folder.
